thread:
Anna R.: drafting SDK guidance for Private/Dedicated customers. need preferred order for KMS creds: cloud identity, Vault, SSM, env. also DEK rotation pattern: lazy vs bulk? what should SDK expose as config?

Marcus H.: prefer cloud identity (IRSA/WorkloadIdentity/MSI) then Vault (transit or short-lived cloud creds), then SSM + KMS-encrypted params, last resort env. avoid long-lived plaintext env vars.

Julia K.: agree. on-prem -> Vault AppRole/mTLS + Transit so apps never see CMKs. if Vault issues cloud creds, ensure CMK key policy trusts assumed role ARN.

Tom O.: SDK should implement a provider chain and allow pinning. proposal: REDWOOD_KMS_PROVIDER=auto|cloud|vault|ssm|env. auto resolves cloud -> vault -> ssm -> env.

Anna R.: sample env snippet for docs: ```
REDWOOD_KMS_PROVIDER=auto
REDWOOD_KMS_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.internal
REDWOOD_KMS_VAULT_ROLE=redwood-app
REDWOOD_KMS_SSM_PREFIX=/redwood/private/
``` ok?

Marcus H.: yes. add enforcement for private installs: if provider=env require REDWOOD_KMS_SECRET_ENCRYPTED=true and console provisioning audit. note: SSM still requires decrypt perms on the CMK that encrypted the param.

DevEx-Liz: error messages should be actionable: "permission denied: needs kms:GenerateDataKey on alias/redwood-service -- see docs: /kb/kms". reduces customer friction.

Julia K.: DEK rotation: prefer lazy rewrap at scale. keep per-object metadata: object_id, cmk_alias, cmk_id, cmk_version, encrypted_dek_ref. bulk rewrap only for small datasets or strict policy.

Marcus H.: operational steps on suspected compromise: create new CMK alias, update policies, run rewrap job (ReEncrypt) or enable lazy rewrap, rotate long-lived creds, audit decrypt events (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs/Key Vault diagnostics), notify compliance/customers. never log plaintext DEKs.

Anna R.: AWS specifics: do we recommend key policy or IAM for granting KMS perms?

Marcus H.: prefer key policy to limit to specific role ARNs. for cross-account, explicitly add the external principal or use a trusted IAM role with sts:AssumeRole. include kms:ReEncrypt* for rewrap jobs.

Julia K.: GCP/Azure notes: GCP -> Workload Identity first, then service accounts with short-lived tokens. perms needed: cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get and useToEncrypt/useToDecrypt. Azure -> MSI first, SPNs only if necessary; Key Vault RBAC: keys/encrypt, keys/decrypt, keys/wrapKey, keys/unwrapKey.

Tom O.: SDK features to surface: reencrpyt_on_write (default false), rewrap_on_read (lazy; default true), and a rewrap_queue for bulk jobs. also expose diagnostic flags that print which provider resolved credentials.

DevEx-Liz: testing checklist for docs: simulate key rotation in staging for each cloud, validate lazy rewrap, test Vault TTL expiry paths, verify audit logs show principal + key alias.

Anna R.: compliance checklist items to include in RFC: CMK rotation cadence (annual baseline), audit log retention (SOC2 = 1yr, some customers 3-7yrs), separation of duties for key-admin vs. key-usage, console restrictions on CMK creation/rotation.

Marcus H.: permission bullets to add in RFC: AWS: kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:DescribeKey. GCP: cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get, cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt, cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt. Azure: keys/encrypt, keys/decrypt, keys/wrapKey, keys/unwrapKey.

Julia K.: infra gotcha: SSM params encrypted with KMS require the app principal to have decrypt permission for the CMK used by the param. create per-service CMKs to avoid blast radius.

Marcus H.: security note: do not log DEK content or derived symmetric keys. log only key aliases/ids and requestor principal. enable CloudTrail KMS events and Key Vault diagnostics.

Anna R.: incident playbook sketch included in RFC?

DevEx-Liz: yes, add short templates for ops -> customers -> legal. also include runbook steps and sample CLI commands for AWS ReEncrypt and Azure rewrap patterns.

Tom O.: add an integration test that spins up Vault Transit in CI and asserts that SDK never exposes CMK material and that ReEncrypt calls occur when expected.
